_readme: IMPORTANT: this file is a reference, not something you upload. MSG91 has no
'import template JSON' feature. The template is registered in two places by
hand — the DLT portal and the MSG91 panel — and MSG91 then gives you a
template_id, which is the only thing the application code needs.
The two texts below must be character-for-character identical apart from the
placeholder syntax ({#var#} on DLT, ##OTP## in MSG91). A single extra space
or a changed full stop and the operator drops the message silently, with a
success response from MSG91. That failure mode is why this file exists.

step_1_dlt_registration.where: Jio / Airtel / Vi / BSNL DLT portal — register once with any one, it propagates

template.content: {#var#} is your OTP to log in to SmartAppt. Valid for 5 minutes. Do not share this code with anyone. - S H Enterprises
notes: 'Service Implicit' is correct for OTP: it does not require the recipient
to have consented, which is what you need for a login code.
Do not choose Promotional — OTPs on a promotional route are blocked by DND.

step_2_msg91_panel.content: ##OTP## is your OTP to log in to SmartAppt. Valid for 5 minutes. Do not share this code with anyone. - S H Enterprises
notes: MSG91 uses ##OTP## where DLT uses {#var#}. Everything else must match.
Saving this returns an MSG91 template_id — a different value from the DLT
template id. The application uses the MSG91 one.

step_3_environment._note: Never commit these. Set them on Railway only.

_notes: mobile is country code + number, no '+' and no spaces. toWaNumber() in
whatsapp.service.ts already produces exactly this shape — reuse it.
Passing 'otp' explicitly makes MSG91 send OUR code rather than generating
its own. That matters: the code is already in Redis via setOtp(), and
verification happens in our own verifyOtp(). Letting MSG91 generate one
would mean two different codes and a login that never succeeds.
otp_expiry is in MINUTES. Our TTL is 300 seconds, hence 5.
send._response_warning: HTTP 200 with type 'error' is normal. Check the body, not the status code.

_why_unused: We verify against Redis in authService.verifyOtp, which also enforces
attempt limits and lockout. Delegating verification to MSG91 would move
that logic out of our control and break the dev bypass.

resend._note: 'voice' reads the code aloud. Useful where SMS is undelivered, but it needs its own DLT approval.

checklist: Send to a number that has never received a SmartAppt message.
Confirm the received text matches the registered template EXACTLY.
Confirm the sender shows as SMAPPT, not a numeric long code.
Check control.msg91.com -> Reports for DELIVERED, not just SUBMITTED.
Test to a DND-registered number — service-implicit should still land.

_unverified: The v5 endpoint paths and parameter names above are from MSG91's public
documentation and community sources; the docs site would not render fully
when this was written. Confirm 'otp_expiry' units and the /otp/retry
parameter names against the panel's own API tester before relying on them.
